text:
dena: Quick sync — planning to enable the feature flag `fastpath_cache_coalesce` for a small prod canary tonight at 22:00 PT. Need eng-runtime + oncall + infra signoff. Purpose: reduce tail latency for short requests by coalescing micro-batches; risk = transient queue spikes and cache thrash.

ajay: Can you confirm the canary audience and exact rollout steps? Also what are hard rollback gates?

dena: Canary = 5% traffic slice (audience id: sff-canary-5). Rollout plan: flip flag -> observe 15m smoke -> ramp to 20% over 30m if green -> keep at 20% for 2h then full ramp. Rollback triggers: p99 latency +10% vs baseline, error rate >0.5%, GPU queue depth +30% sustained, or any OOMs.

leo: Add these to the checklist: tokens/sec per GPU, KV cache hit rate, and redis/memcached eviction rate. If cache hit rate drops by >8% that’s a red flag.

dena: Agreed. Primary dashboards: latency (per-route p50/p95/p99), gpu-queue-depth, tokens/sec, kv-hit-rate, eviction-rate. Dash links: https://console.redwood/dashboards/fastpath-canary and traces: https://console.redwood/traces?q=fastpath

alex: I can run the smoke script right after the flip: `./scripts/smoke_fastpath.sh --target canary`. Will post results (latency histograms + a few sample traces).

ajay: Who is flipping the flag and where is the runbook? I want a one-line rollback command we can run from the pager.

dena: I'll flip it. Rollback command (ops):
```
redwood-ops flag set --name fastpath_cache_coalesce --state disabled --audience sff-canary-5 --reason "rollback: <reason>"
```
Manual global rollback (if needed):
```
redwood-ops flag set --name fastpath_cache_coalesce --state disabled --audience all
```
Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/rollouts/fastpath-cache-coalesce

sre-bot: scheduled monitor group created -> monitors: fastpath-canary-latency, fastpath-canary-error-rate, fastpath-gpu-queue. Pager escalation configured.

leo: For safety, enable a short hysteresis window on the gate (3m) and cap ramp step to 20% per step. Also set a max concurrent reqs per worker limit to avoid overload during bursts.

dena: Good call. Hysteresis = 3m, ramp step = 20%. Concurrency cap set via config `worker.max_inflight = 8` for canary. I'll push config change first, then flip flag.

ajay: What about data plane fallback? If the fastpath fails for a request, will there be an automatic fallback to baseline path?

dena: Yes — requests that error on fastpath will fall back to the standard execution path with a logged tag `fastpath-fallback=true`. We’ll watch traces for fallback ratio; rollback if fallback % > 5%.

alex: After smoke I’ll paste 15m histograms and a sample trace id. If anything looks off I’ll tag `@dena` and `@leo`.

dena: Thanks. Final checklist for tonight:
- push `worker.max_inflight` config to canary cluster (dena)
- flip flag to sff-canary-5 at 22:00 PT (dena)
- run `./scripts/smoke_fastpath.sh` (alex)
- monitor dashboards for 15m (ajay, leo, oncall)
- rollback on triggers listed above (anyone)

sre-bot: note: oncall person for window = @ajay (22:00-00:00 PT).

ajay: I’ll be on pager duty and watching the dashboards. If I see sustained queueing or p99 regressed beyond threshold I’ll run the rollback command.

dena: Great — I’ll post start/stop updates in this thread. Ping me here if you need to abort early. :thumbsup:

alex: ACK, will post smoke results.

leo: LGTM from infra side.

sre-bot: action: create incident channel if rollback triggered -> #incident-fastpath-2123456789
